examples.title: ANALGWST POINT3, continuous point source
examples.source: ANALGWST (analytical groundwater solute transport code), version 1.1
examples.compares: Concentration on the printed grid at each printed time and depth, decay 0 and 0.03 per day, against the program output.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the last printed decimal: 5e-7 absolute (test bound 5.1e-7), plus 1e-9 relative.

examples.title: ANALGWST PATCHI, patch source on the inflow plane
examples.source: ANALGWST (analytical groundwater solute transport code), version 1.1
examples.compares: Concentration on the printed grid at each printed time and depth, decay 0 and 0.01 per day, against the program output.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the last printed decimal: 5e-7 absolute (test bound 5.1e-7), plus 1e-9 relative.

examples.title: ANALGWST PATCHF, finite aquifer with no-flux boundaries
examples.source: ANALGWST (analytical groundwater solute transport code), version 1.1
examples.compares: Concentration on the printed grid at each printed time and depth in a 60 m wide, 10 m thick aquifer, decay 0 and 0.01 per day, against the program output.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the last printed decimal: 5e-6 absolute (test bound 5.1e-6), plus 1e-9 relative.

examples.title: mibitrans Bioscreen, truncated Domenico solution
examples.source: mibitrans
examples.compares: The truncated Domenico plume concentration at sampled (x, y, t) points against the package output.
examples.tolerance: 1e-9 absolute plus 1e-9 relative.

examples.title: mibitrans Mibitrans, exact patch solution
examples.source: mibitrans
examples.compares: The exact Wexler patch solution (no source depletion) at the same sampled points against the package output.
examples.tolerance: 1e-10 absolute plus 1e-7 relative.

examples.title: SSG 1996 Table A-1, generic soil-to-groundwater levels
examples.source: Soil Screening Guidance: Technical Background Document
examples.compares: The MCL-based generic level at DAF 20 and DAF 1 for 15 chemicals. It checks the three-phase partition formula, the DAF arithmetic and the metal Kd values; the organic Koc and H were read from Tables 36 and 39 of the document on 2026-10-21.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the last printed digit: two significant figures from 10 up, one below 10.

examples.title: RSL November 2024 resident tap water, combined levels
examples.source: Regional Screening Levels (RSLs), Generic Tables, November 2024
examples.compares: The carcinogenic and child noncarcinogenic tap water levels over ingestion and bathing dermal, back-calculated by the cleanup solver. A blank cell is asserted as no level.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the second significant figure.

examples.title: RSL November 2024 risk-based soil-to-groundwater SSL
examples.source: Regional Screening Levels (RSLs), Generic Tables, November 2024
examples.compares: The DAF 1 risk-based SSL for the six chemicals with no household-use inhalation term: the unrounded lower tap water level times the partition factor.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the second significant figure.

examples.title: Table R-9, direct exposure pathways (page 1 of 3)
examples.source: Review of Risk Integrated Software for Cleanups (RISC) v4.0
examples.compares: Dose, cancer risk and hazard index for soil ingestion, soil dermal contact, groundwater ingestion and shower dermal contact, for four chemicals. A printed NQ is asserted as a null. The table lists no exposure inputs; the RISC4 manual values are fixture inputs for this case only, and the dermal soil rows use a back-solved product of 5,750.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the last printed digit, derived from the printed string.
examples.note: This reproduces the review arithmetic and is not evidence of model accuracy.

examples.title: RSL November 2024, independent check of the modern method
examples.source: Regional Screening Levels (RSLs), Generic Tables, November 2024
examples.compares: Resident soil, composite worker soil, resident tap water and resident air screening levels at target risk 1e-6 and hazard quotient 1. A blank cell is asserted as no coefficient.
examples.tolerance: The engine value rounds to the published value: half a unit in the second significant figure.

examples.title: RSL November 2024 default exposure parameters
examples.source: Regional Screening Levels (RSLs), Generic Tables, November 2024
examples.compares: The modern resident and composite worker presets, the ADAF age segments and the sheet’s own age-adjusted factors.
examples.casesUnit: age-adjusted factors (the preset values are compared as well)
examples.tolerance: Equal to the printed precision of each factor (toBeCloseTo at 1 to 6 decimals).

examples.title: SSG 1996 Table 3-A, soil saturation limits
examples.source: Soil Screening Guidance: Technical Background Document
examples.compares: The soil saturation limit Csat for six chemicals with the document’s default soil.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the second printed significant figure (per-chemical bound in the file).

examples.title: BIOSCREEN soluble mass example
examples.source: BIOSCREEN natural attenuation decision support system, user's manual
examples.compares: The initial soluble mass of three zones, M0 = F rho_b H_s A.
examples.tolerance: 0.5 kg absolute (the printed masses are rounded to kg).

examples.title: Saturated soil source constructed cases A and B
examples.source: Constructed cases computed by an independent script from the equations of the methods note; not a published example.
examples.compares: Depletion times, rates and initial masses of a source with and without a separate phase and a fluctuating water table.
examples.tolerance: 1e-9 relative (arithmetic); initial mass 1e-12.
examples.note: An arithmetic cross-check, not a comparison with a published value.

examples.title: Table R-8, river and lake mixing
examples.source: Review of Risk Integrated Software for Cleanups (RISC) v4.0
examples.compares: Groundwater flow, mass flux, the river and lake concentrations and the sediment concentration. The RISC4 benzene Koc is a fixture input for this case only.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the last printed digit (0.005 mg/L, 0.005 mg/kg, 0.5 mg/d).
examples.note: The review reports exact agreement with its own hand calculation, so this reproduces arithmetic, not model accuracy.

examples.title: RISC5 user’s guide Appendix L, river and lake examples
examples.source: RISC5 user’s guide, Appendix L (not a references.json record).
examples.compares: The river (30.8 mg/L) and lake (11.7 mg/L) concentrations. The adjusted-volume lake example is not used.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the last printed digit (0.05 mg/L).

examples.title: Table R-2, probabilistic drinking water case
examples.source: Review of Risk Integrated Software for Cleanups (RISC) v4.0
examples.compares: The legacy method runs the printed case with body weight, exposure duration and water ingestion sampled, and the test asserts no failed iteration and monotone, non-degenerate percentiles. The printed percentiles are recorded and not compared, because the review gives no input distributions.
examples.tolerance: None. No printed value is compared.
examples.note: A comparison waits for sourced input distributions.

examples.title: Table R-7, vadose leaching to the water table
examples.source: Review of Risk Integrated Software for Cleanups (RISC) v4.0
examples.compares: The source pore water concentration and the water table concentration at 10 years (mean of the twelve month-end values of year 10). Benzene properties are RISC4 values used for this case only.
examples.tolerance: 1 percent (source pore water) and 3 percent (water table) relative.
examples.note: The water table value is ill-conditioned (5 percent on Koc moves it about 25 percent), so this reproduces the review arithmetic and is not evidence of model accuracy.

examples.title: van Genuchten and Alves 1982 Table 6, program A1 output
examples.source: Analytical solutions of the one-dimensional convective-dispersive solute transport equation
examples.compares: Concentration against distance at five times for the first-type and third-type inlets, without decay or depletion.
examples.tolerance: 5e-5 absolute (four decimals as printed).
examples.note: One first-type value (t = 10, x = 14) has a degraded printed glyph and is entered as the closed form reads it.

examples.title: Tables R-3, R-4 and R-5, vapor intrusion
examples.source: Review of Risk Integrated Software for Cleanups (RISC) v4.0
examples.compares: Soil to indoor air with and without TPH (R-3), the dominant layer with degradation (R-4) and groundwater to indoor air (R-5). The independent column of R-3 is recorded, not asserted.
examples.tolerance: 0.5 percent of the RISC value (the test asserts it seven times: the six printed results and a second run of R-3 case A without degradation).

examples.title: Table R-6, groundwater to outdoor air
examples.source: Review of Risk Integrated Software for Cleanups (RISC) v4.0
examples.compares: The printed 2.27e-3 mg/m^3 equals the indoor result of Table R-5 to three figures and no box reading reproduces it (the box gives 2.54e-6 mg/m^3). It is treated as a transcription error in the review. The box hand value is asserted instead.
examples.tolerance: The box hand value at 1e-9 relative; the printed value is never widened into a tolerance.
examples.note: Not reproduced; the printed value is believed to be a transcription error.

examples.title: RISC5 user’s guide Appendix J, layered vapor example
examples.source: RISC5 user’s guide, Appendix J (not a references.json record).
examples.compares: The normalized concentration at the top of layer 1 for the base, dry and wet cases. The values are stated in prose from figures, so they are figure readings.
examples.tolerance: 0.01 absolute.

examples.title: EPA 2004 Appendix C, SL-ADV benzene worked example
examples.source: User's Guide for Evaluating Subsurface Vapor Intrusion into Buildings
examples.compares: Printed intermediate and final values of the spreadsheet example: building geometry, ventilation, permeability, effective diffusion, source vapor, and the mass-limited building concentration.
examples.tolerance: Half a unit in the last printed digit of each value (the test derives it from the printed string).

examples.title: VISL screening levels, identity check
examples.source: Vapor Intrusion Screening Level User's Guide
examples.compares: The online VISL calculator was not run, so no printed VISL value is asserted. The test checks identity 8c (groundwater screening level times AF times H times 1000 L/m^3 equals the target indoor air) against the RSL resident air values.
examples.tolerance: 1e-12 relative (an identity, not a published value).
examples.note: Pending a run of the VISL calculator.

examples.title: Eco-SSL wildlife derivation, cadmium and lead surrogate rows
examples.source: Ecological Soil Screening Levels (Eco-SSLs)
examples.compares: The soil concentration at which the wildlife hazard quotient is 1, back-calculated from the transcribed derivation inputs of the printed surrogate rows, against the printed wildlife Eco-SSL. Avian (dove, woodcock, hawk) and mammalian (vole, shrew, weasel) surrogates for cadmium and lead.
examples.tolerance: 5 percent relative (a ruling, DECISIONS.md entry 10 of the Eco-SSL milestone).
examples.note: The derivation inputs come from the transcribed Eco-SSL data, so this checks the back-calculation arithmetic against the printed values, not the inputs.

examples.title: Eco-SSL wildlife guild values, cadmium mammalian and lead avian
examples.source: Ecological Soil Screening Levels (Eco-SSLs)
examples.compares: The smallest surrogate value of the guild against the printed guild Eco-SSL: 0.36 mg/kg for cadmium (mammalian) and 11 mg/kg for lead (avian).
examples.tolerance: 5 percent relative (the same ruling as the surrogate rows).

examples.title: SSG 1996 default particulate emission factor
examples.source: Soil Screening Guidance: Technical Background Document
examples.compares: The default PEF of 1.32E9 m^3/kg from the printed wind erosion inputs.
examples.tolerance: Equal to the printed three significant figures (1.32e9).

examples.title: SSG 2002 default particulate emission factor
examples.source: Supplemental Guidance for Developing Soil Screening Levels for Superfund Sites
examples.compares: The default PEF of 1.36E9 m^3/kg with Q/C 93.77.
examples.tolerance: Equal to the printed three significant figures (1.36e9).

examples.title: NRWQC zinc criteria at a hardness of 100 mg/L
examples.source: National Recommended Water Quality Criteria - Aquatic Life Criteria Table
examples.compares: The hardness-dependent acute and chronic freshwater zinc criteria computed from the Appendix B slope, intercept and conversion factor against the published 117.2 and 118.1 ug/L.
examples.tolerance: Within 0.5 ug/L (toBeCloseTo at zero decimals), and the acute value rounds to 120 at two significant figures.

examples.title: Table R-7, unit-gradient moisture content
examples.source: Review of Risk Integrated Software for Cleanups (RISC) v4.0
examples.compares: The moisture content that carries 20 cm/yr in the vadose soil (theta 0.0885) and in the lens (theta 0.2031) with the Brooks and Corey relative permeability.
examples.tolerance: 1e-4 absolute (four decimals as printed).

examples.title: EPA 2004 Appendix C, benzene Henry constant at the system temperature
examples.source: User's Guide for Evaluating Subsurface Vapor Intrusion into Buildings
examples.compares: The enthalpy of vaporization at 10 degrees C (8,122 cal/mol), the Henry constant (2.68e-3 atm m^3/mol) and the dimensionless constant (0.115) of the spreadsheet example.
examples.tolerance: The printed digits: the enthalpy rounds to the integer, the two constants to three significant figures. The unrounded values are pinned to 1e-9 relative.

examples.title: Table R-9, Inhalation in Shower
examples.source: Review of Risk Integrated Software for Cleanups (RISC) v4.0
examples.compares: The shower model inputs of the review (droplet size, fall time, water flow, stall volume, film coefficients, water temperature) are not printed in the table or in the RISC5 guide, and the RISC4 manual that carries them was not available, so the row cannot be reproduced without inventing inputs. The shower model is checked by identities and hand cases instead.
examples.tolerance: Not compared. Checked by identities and hand cases instead.
examples.note: Ruling recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-18, M7 slice E4, item 4.

examples.title: Table R-9, Ingestion of Root Vegetables (M9)
examples.source: Review of Risk Integrated Software for Cleanups (RISC) v4.0
examples.compares: The root vegetable ingestion row of the page-1 table is not reproduced yet.
examples.tolerance: Not compared yet.

examples.title: van Genuchten and Alves 1982 Table 6, eight named exceptions
examples.source: Analytical solutions of the one-dimensional convective-dispersive solute transport equation
examples.compares: Eight printed values the 1982 program evidently evaluated slightly differently at large x and t: first-type t = 5, x = 18 and seven third-type points. Each is asserted at the widened bound, and the other values stay at 5e-5.
examples.tolerance: 0.00015 absolute, by name (ruling in docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-16: M2 tolerance rulings (Named exceptions at 1.5e-4)).
examples.note: The closed form agrees with the printed values only to 1.5e-4 at these points.

defaults.subject: Foster and Chrostowski film reference coefficients (3000 cm/h gas, 20 cm/h liquid)
defaults.note: RISC5 choices that could not be verified against the primary paper; they are inputs and the defaults are warned. The stagnant stall source is a planned, unverified record and is not cited.

defaults.subject: Little (1992) two-resistance stall mass balance
defaults.note: The mass balance is our statement of the two-resistance theory, checked by limit identities; it is not a transcription of the paper.

defaults.subject: Household transfer factor K (RSL whole-house water-to-air term)
defaults.note: An entered value that could not be verified against a primary page of the RSL documentation. Table 1 of the archived RSL User's Guide (19january2021snapshot.epa.gov/risk/regional-screening-levels-rsls-users-guide_.html, read 2026-10-21) lists K, the Andelman volatilization factor, as 0.5 L/m3, citing U.S. EPA 1991b (pg. 20). The equation form (C_a = C_w K) is not confirmed, because the page prints its equations as images, so the warning stays.

defaults.subject: HHRAP fallback standing in for Trapp (2015)
defaults.note: The modern plant model is the EPA HHRAP 2005 produce equations until the Trapp (2015) models are read.

defaults.subject: Transpiration stream concentration factor (TSCF) and leaf-air partition coefficient
defaults.note: User inputs, because their published regressions were not read.

defaults.subject: Briggs root concentration factor constants
defaults.note: The constants 0.77 and -1.52 were read in the paper itself on 2026-10-21 (Pestic. Sci. 13, 495-504, open copy in the Rothamsted repository, page 500, Equations 1 and 2; the TSCF equation is on page 502). The engine's form drops the paper's 0.82 term above log Kow 2, as the HHRAP appendix does: Equation 1 is the macerated-root line, and Equation 2 adds 0.82 to the root concentration factor at every log Kow.

defaults.subject: Schulze-Makuch (2005) dispersivity coefficients
defaults.note: The unconsolidated-media pair c = 0.20, m = 0.44 is quoted from lecture notes that cite the paper, not from the paper’s own tables.

defaults.subject: Gelhar et al. (1985) two-branch vadose dispersivity regression
defaults.note: The coefficients have no primary source located: the EPRI report (EA-4190, full text read 2026-10-21) prints no regression equation, only field data and a plot against scale. They come from RISC5’s statement of its choice. The reference stays cited for the field data compilation it does contain.

defaults.subject: Organic Koc and H of the SSG 1996 Table A-1 fixture
defaults.note: The nine organic Koc values (Table 39, calculated Koc) and H (Table 36, dimensionless) were read from the primary document on 2026-10-21 and match, after correcting PCE H to 0.754. Table C-1 of the User's Guide and the inorganic Kd values were not re-read.

notChecked.subject: RSL inhalation cells
notChecked.note: Tap water inhalation, soil inhalation and the noncancer worker air value of the RSL tables are not checked by the RSL independent check; the benzo(a)pyrene tap water dermal value is omitted by the RSL and has no case.

notChecked.subject: DeVaull (2007) vapor model
notChecked.note: No published numeric example could be verified, so the model rests on identities and hand cases built from independent closed forms. There is no fixture file.

notChecked.subject: Table R-9 pages 2 and 3
notChecked.note: The RISC5 guide reproduces only page 1 of the three pages, so the other rows cannot be checked.
